sources.title: Study guide for Exam GH-300: GitHub Copilot
sources.contentRelevance: Current GH-300 objective taxonomy effective August 7, 2026: six weighted domains, fourteen skills, and forty-one subskills. Authoritative current taxonomy only; resources link to both permitted and prohibited domains, so guide linkage alone is not sufficient for technical evidence approval.

sources.title: Reviewing audit logs for GitHub Copilot

parents.evidenceSummary: Actual parent passage: "Utilize audit log events".
parents.relevanceJustification: This article directly concerns Copilot audit log events, with enterprise-owner scope explicitly preserved instead of assuming organization-owner equivalence.

sources.contentRelevance: Enterprise Copilot audit access, event filters, exclusion of local prompt data, 180-day retention, and streaming for longer-term history. Enterprise owners or the Read enterprise audit logs custom role; Business or Enterprise. Do not generalize these roles to organization audit permissions.

sources.title: Application card: GitHub Copilot Chat

parents.evidenceSummary: Actual parent passage: "Understand the limits, options, feedback, and commands of GitHub Copilot Chat; include prompt file reuse for consistent responses".
parents.relevanceJustification: The Chat application card provides the limits and response-processing behavior of the explicitly named feature; use only sections tied to Chat and PR summaries.

sources.contentRelevance: Chat input processing, surface-specific context, BYOK data considerations, incomplete or inaccurate outputs, and on-demand PR summaries with a large-file limit. Approve only claim-inventory sections covering Chat context, output validation, PR summaries, and provider data scope. Do not infer product availability, legal ownership, or fixed retention from this application card.

sources.title: About GitHub Copilot CLI

parents.evidenceSummary: Actual parent passage: "Define GitHub Copilot CLI and how it benefits developers".
parents.relevanceJustification: The article defines the named CLI product and its terminal capabilities; permission details are relevant to operating that CLI responsibly.

sources.contentRelevance: Standalone CLI interactive/programmatic modes, context management, heuristic trusted-directory boundaries, and allow/deny tool permissions. Use stable CLI modes and permission semantics in the inventory. First-party cloud/local sandboxes are Public Preview and not used by these claims. No blanket model-window size or assurance of security isolation is approved.

sources.title: Getting started with GitHub Copilot CLI

parents.evidenceSummary: Actual parent passage: "Identify the steps for installing GitHub Copilot CLI". The canonical redirect chain is preserved in the indexed receipt.
parents.relevanceJustification: The objective explicitly asks about installing the CLI; this article supplies installation prerequisites, package commands, and authentication.

sources.contentRelevance: Standalone CLI npm/WinGet installation, Node.js prerequisite, organization policy prerequisite, initial login, and programmatic prompt flags. Current standalone Copilot CLI only; do not substitute legacy gh copilot extension commands. Initial approval behavior assumes no automatic-approval override.

sources.title: Using GitHub Copilot CLI

parents.evidenceSummary: Actual parent passage: "Use GitHub Copilot CLI interactively and in sessions".
parents.relevanceJustification: The usage overview covers the exact interactive CLI sessions named by this subskill, including session context and approval.

sources.contentRelevance: CLI file context, session resumption, directory changes, direct shell execution, tool approval choices, and specialized subagents. Current CLI. Read exact permission and session constraints. Do not infer that all customization surfaces or model capabilities are available in every host.

sources.title: Content exclusion for GitHub Copilot

parents.evidenceSummary: Actual parent passage: "Configure content exclusions and editor settings".
parents.relevanceJustification: This objective specifically names content exclusions; the article describes precisely their supported environments and boundaries, not unrelated privacy subjects.

sources.contentRelevance: Business/Enterprise exclusion behavior, supported-mode limitations, indirect semantic information, symlinks, remote filesystems, and policy lookup. Inventory uses GA local supported IDE inline/Chat behavior only. GitHub website and Mobile exclusions are explicitly Public Preview. Editor Edit/Agent modes are unsupported. Icon-only support-matrix cells are not evidence.

sources.title: Excluding content from GitHub Copilot

parents.evidenceSummary: Actual parent passage: "Configure content exclusions and editor settings".
parents.relevanceJustification: This exact how-to implements the guide's named exclusion configuration subskill, documenting enterprise, organization, and repository scopes and IDE rule updates.

sources.contentRelevance: Exclusion administration roles, inherited rules, enterprise versus organization scope, path patterns, propagation, and supported-IDE tests. Business/Enterprise and supported modes only. Repository Maintain is view-only. Do not treat exclusion as a universal security or confidentiality boundary.

sources.title: Application card: GitHub Copilot inline suggestions

parents.evidenceSummary: Actual parent passage: "Visualize code suggestion lifecycle".
parents.relevanceJustification: The inline-suggestion application card describes prompt processing, model inference, filtering, and the lifecycle of the named code suggestions.

sources.contentRelevance: Inline suggestion lifecycle, cursor/open-file context, explicit acceptance, model limitations, code matching, and review requirements. Use behavior and limitations, not the contradictory plan banner or broad natural-language scope wording. Internal evaluation descriptions are not selected as claim authority.

sources.title: Adding repository custom instructions for GitHub Copilot

parents.evidenceSummary: Actual parent passage: "Utilize Spaces, Spark, Pull Request summaries, and customizable review standards via instructions files".
parents.relevanceJustification: This article covers repository instruction files used to customize Copilot review standards, including file scope and code-review limitations.

sources.contentRelevance: Repository and path-specific instruction files, applyTo and excludeAgent, combined context, and head-branch instructions in PR reviews. The current article says review instructions are read from the head branch. Older base-branch or 4,000-character assumptions are not approved. On GitHub.com, path-specific instructions are limited to cloud agent and code review.

sources.title: Managing policies and features for GitHub Copilot in your organization

parents.evidenceSummary: Actual parent passage: "Configure organization-wide policy management; enable Copilot Code Review policies and manage feature availability across IDEs and github.com".
parents.relevanceJustification: The organization policy article covers that exact administrative scope and feature enablement, not unrelated enterprise governance.

sources.contentRelevance: Organization owner feature/model policy controls, enterprise enforcement precedence, and opt-in preview settings. Business/Enterprise organization scope; inherited enterprise settings cannot be overridden. The existence of a preview opt-in does not make all preview features GA.

sources.title: Managing GitHub Copilot policies as an individual subscriber

parents.evidenceSummary: Actual parent passage: "Enable suggestions matching public code filtering".
parents.relevanceJustification: The individual policy article documents the explicitly requested public-code matching control and whether organization settings can constrain it.

sources.contentRelevance: Public-code matching controls, inherited organizational settings, and individual versus Business/Enterprise model-training settings. Public-code Block mode applies only where supported. Data claims are scoped to plan and current policy, not blanket retention or legal guarantees.

sources.title: Plans for GitHub Copilot

parents.evidenceSummary: Actual parent passage: "GitHub Copilot plans and features". Original link: https://docs.github.com/copilot/about-github-copilot/plans-for-github-copilot. The canonical redirect chain is preserved in the indexed receipt.
parents.relevanceJustification: The study guide directly links the Copilot plan comparison; limit authority to plan availability and plan administration.

sources.contentRelevance: Current plan comparison: Business adds centralized management; Enterprise is for GitHub Enterprise Cloud; Copilot is not available for Enterprise Server. Current billing uses AI credits. Use prose plan distinctions only. Icon-only feature matrix cells were not preserved in main-text extraction. Do not use its Spark listing to override the blocked Spark article redirect. Model-specific preview features and pricing amounts are outside this claim inventory.

sources.contentRelevance: Goal/constraint prompts, input-output examples, task decomposition, relevant files, iteration, and focused conversation history. Prompt-design guidance, not guarantees of semantic correctness. Linked blogs were not fetched or used.
